fact_check.note: The trial only enrolled 8 participants total. The denominators (7, 8, 4) reflect how many participants reached each specific dose level during the study.

research_page.title: Etalanetug (E2814) in dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease (Phase 1b/2)
research_page.description: An open-label Phase 1b/2 trial evaluating safety and target engagement of the anti-tau antibody etalanetug in eight people with dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease.
research_page.takeaway_md: Etalanetug demonstrated strong target engagement by substantially reducing CSF tau biomarkers in a very small study. However, severe adverse events emerged at higher doses, underscoring the need for safety validation in larger ongoing trials.
key_findings_md: Substantial reductions in CSF tau biomarkers at Day 757, including MTBR-tau243 (-381), p-tau181 (-606.64), and p-tau217 (-422.60) ([registry data](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04971733)).
Serious adverse events occurred at higher dose levels, including cerebral venous sinus thrombosis and seizure in the 3000 mg group ([registry data](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04971733)).
research_page.methods_md: Open-label Phase 1b/2 trial enrolling 8 adults with mild to moderate cognitive impairment due to dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease (NCT04971733). Participants received intravenous etalanetug with intra-patient dose escalation up to 4500 mg over 120 weeks.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: This Phase 1b/2 trial ([NCT04971733](/trials/e2814-nct04971733)) provides early biomarker validation following a Phase 1 healthy volunteer study ([NCT04231513](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04231513)). Because of the extremely small sample size and lack of placebo control, clinical efficacy cannot be established here. Etalanetug is currently being evaluated in larger controlled trials, including the DIAN-TU Phase 2/3 platform trial ([NCT05269394](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05269394)) and a Phase 2 study in early Alzheimer's disease ([NCT06602258](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)).
research_page.sentiment_md: Scientific discussion reflects cautious optimism. Experts are encouraged by robust biomarker responses but heavily emphasize the risks of severe adverse events and the limitations of an n=8 sample. The broader patient and caregiver communities remain largely unaware of this early-stage asset.
caveats_md: The extremely small sample size (n=8) limits statistical power and prevents definitive conclusions regarding the drug's safety profile.
The open-label design lacks a placebo control, making it difficult to confidently attribute specific outcomes directly to the intervention.
relates_to_md: [Biomarkers](/research/biomarkers) — Evaluates novel tau biomarkers including MTBR-tau243.

trial_pages.title: E2814 Phase 1b/2 in DIAD
trial_pages.description: Open-label safety and target engagement study of etalanetug in 8 participants with dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.population: Adults with mild to moderate cognitive impairment due to dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Number of participants with TEAEs/SAEs and change from baseline in CSF MTBR-tau
trial_pages.why_md: This trial was designed to establish basic safety, tolerability, and biomarker target engagement for etalanetug in a patient population before proceeding to larger efficacy studies.
trial_pages.results_md: Etalanetug demonstrated target engagement with dose-dependent reductions in CSF tau biomarkers (MTBR-tau, p-tau181, p-tau217). Treatment-emergent adverse events were observed across dose groups, including serious adverse events at the 3000 mg and 4500 mg dose levels, in a small cohort of 8 participants.
